sanskrit: pāṇḍavānāṃ kurūṇāṃ ca parasparasamāgame te sene bhṛśasaṃvigne yayatuḥ svaṃ niveśanam
english: At the clash of the Pāṇḍavas and the Kurus, each against the other, both armies, sorely shaken, withdrew to their own encampments.

sanskrit: tataḥ svaśibiraṃ gatvā nyaviśaṃs tatra bhārata pāṇḍavāḥ sṛñjayaiḥ sārdhaṃ kuravaś ca yathāvidhi
english: Then, having gone each to its own camp, they settled there, O Bhārata—the Pāṇḍavas together with the Sṛñjayas, and the Kurus likewise, in due order.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vihṛtya ca tato rājan sahitāḥ kurupāṇḍavāḥ vyatītāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ punar yuddhāya niryayuḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having rested through the night, O king, the Kurus and Pāṇḍavas together, when the dark watch had passed, marched forth once more to battle.

sanskrit: tatra śabdo mahān āsīt tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata yujyatāṃ rathamukhyānāṃ kalpyatāṃ caiva dantinām
english: There arose a mighty din, O Bhārata, among your forces and among theirs, as the foremost chariots were yoked and the tusked elephants made ready.

sanskrit: saṃnahyatāṃ padātīnāṃ hayānāṃ caiva bhārata śaṅkhadundubhinādaś ca tumulaḥ sarvato 'bhavat
english: As the foot soldiers armed themselves and the horses too, O Bhārata, a tumultuous blare of conches and kettledrums rose up on every side.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā dhṛṣṭadyumnam abhāṣata vyūhaṃ vyūha mahābāho makaraṃ śatrutāpanam
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira addressed Dhṛṣṭadyumna: O mighty-armed one, scorcher of foes, array the host in the form of the Makara, the sea-monster.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu pārthena dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ vyādideśa mahārāja rathino rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Thus addressed by Pārtha, the great chariot-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna, O great king, the best of chariot-fighters, gave his commands to the warriors.

sanskrit: śiro 'bhūd drupadas tasya pāṇḍavaś ca dhanaṃjayaḥ cakṣuṣī sahadevaś ca nakulaś ca mahārathaḥ tuṇḍam āsīn mahārāja bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ
english: Drupada, with the Pāṇḍava Dhanaṃjaya, formed its head; Sahadeva and the great chariot-warrior Nakula were its two eyes; and the mighty Bhīmasena, O great king, was its snout.

sanskrit: saubhadro draupadeyāś ca rākṣasaś ca ghaṭotkacaḥ sātyakir dharmarājaś ca vyūhagrīvāṃ samāsthitāḥ
english: The son of Subhadrā, the sons of Draupadī, the Rākṣasa Ghaṭotkaca, Sātyaki, and the King of Righteousness took their stand at the neck of the formation.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭham āsīn mahārāja virāṭo vāhinīpatiḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnena sahito mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ
english: At the back, O great king, stood Virāṭa, lord of armies, together with Dhṛṣṭadyumna, surrounded by a great host.

sanskrit: kekayā bhrātaraḥ pañca vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ samāśritāḥ dhṛṣṭaketur naravyāghraḥ karakarṣaś ca vīryavān dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritya sthitā vyūhasya rakṣaṇe
english: The five Kekaya brothers held the left flank; while Dhṛṣṭaketu, tiger among men, and the valiant Karakarṣa, taking the right wing, stood to guard the formation.

sanskrit: pādayos tu mahārāja sthitaḥ śrīmān mahārathaḥ kuntibhojaḥ śatānīko mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ
english: At the two feet, O great king, stood the illustrious great chariot-warriors Kuntibhoja and Śatānīka, encircled by a mighty host.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu maheṣvāsaḥ somakaiḥ saṃvṛto balī irāvāṃś ca tataḥ pucche makarasya vyavasthitau
english: And the mighty bowman Śikhaṇḍī, ringed about by the Somakas, together with Irāvat, took his post at the tail of the Makara.

sanskrit: evam etan mahāvyūhaṃ vyūhya bhārata pāṇḍavāḥ sūryodaye mahārāja punar yuddhāya daṃśitāḥ
english: Having arrayed this great formation thus, O Bhārata, the Pāṇḍavas, mailed and armored at sunrise, stood ready once more for battle, O great king.

sanskrit: kauravān abhyayus tūrṇaṃ hastyaśvarathapattibhiḥ samucchritair dhvajaiś citraiḥ śastraiś ca vimalaiḥ śitaiḥ
english: Swiftly they advanced upon the Kauravas with elephants, horses, chariots, and foot, with banners raised aloft and varied, and with weapons gleaming and keen.

sanskrit: vyūhaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu tat sainyaṃ pitā devavratas tava krauñcena mahatā rājan pratyavyūhata vāhinīm
english: Beholding that arrayed host, your father Devavrata, O king, drew up his own army in counter-formation as a great Krauñca, the heron.

sanskrit: tasya tuṇḍe maheṣvāso bhāradvājo vyarocata aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva cakṣur āstāṃ nareśvara
english: At its beak shone the mighty bowman Bhāradvāja; and Aśvatthāman and Kṛpa were its two eyes, O lord of men.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu sahitaḥ kāmbojāraṭṭabāhlikaiḥ śirasy āsīn naraśreṣṭhaḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sarvadhanuṣmatām
english: And Kṛtavarman, best among men and foremost of all bowmen, joined by the Kāmbojas, the Araṭṭas, and the Bāhlikas, stood at the head.

sanskrit: grīvāyāṃ śūrasenas tu tava putraś ca māriṣa duryodhano mahārāja rājabhir bahubhir vṛtaḥ
english: At the neck stood Śūrasena and your son Duryodhana, O honored one, O great king, surrounded by many kings.

sanskrit: prāgjyotiṣas tu sahitaḥ madrasauvīrakekayaiḥ urasy abhūn naraśreṣṭha mahatyā senayā vṛtaḥ
english: The lord of Prāgjyotiṣa, together with the Madras, Sauvīras, and Kekayas, held the breast, O best of men, encircled by a great host.

sanskrit: svasenayā ca sahitaḥ suśarmā prasthalādhipaḥ vāmaṃ pakṣaṃ samāśritya daṃśitaḥ samavasthitaḥ
english: Suśarman, lord of Prasthala, with his own troops, took the left wing and stood there mailed and ready.

sanskrit: tuṣārā yavanāś caiva śakāś ca saha cūcupaiḥ dakṣiṇaṃ pakṣam āśritya sthitā vyūhasya bhārata
english: The Tuṣāras, the Yavanas, and the Śakas, together with the Cūcupas, holding the right wing, stood guard over the formation, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śrutāyuś ca śatāyuś ca saumadattiś ca māriṣa vyūhasya jaghane tasthū rakṣamāṇāḥ parasparam
english: Śrutāyus, Śatāyus, and the son of Somadatta, O honored one, took their stand at the rear of the array, guarding one another.

sanskrit: tato yuddhāya saṃjagmuḥ pāṇḍavāḥ kauravaiḥ saha sūryodaye mahārāja tato yuddham abhūn mahat
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas closed with the Kauravas for battle at sunrise, O great king, and thereupon a mighty combat began.

sanskrit: pratīyū rathino nāgān nāgāś ca rathino yayuḥ hayārohā hayārohān rathinaś cāpi sādinaḥ
english: Chariot-warriors charged the elephants, and elephants advanced upon the chariots; horsemen rushed at horsemen, and chariot-fighters at riders.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ ca rathī rājan kuñjarāṃś ca mahāraṇe hastyārohā rathārohān rathinaś cāpi sādinaḥ
english: And the chariot-warrior fell upon the charioteer and upon the elephants in that great battle, O king; the elephant-riders fell upon the chariot-riders, and the chariot-fighters upon the horsemen.

sanskrit: rathinaḥ pattibhiḥ sārdhaṃ sādinaś cāpi pattibhiḥ anyonyaṃ samare rājan pratyadhāvann amarṣitāḥ
english: Chariot-fighters with foot soldiers, and horsemen too with foot soldiers, charged at one another in the fray, O king, beside themselves with fury.

sanskrit: bhīmasenārjunayamair guptā cānyair mahārathaiḥ śuśubhe pāṇḍavī senā nakṣatrair iva śarvarī
english: Guarded by Bhīmasena, Arjuna, the twins, and other great chariot-warriors, the army of the Pāṇḍavas shone like the night adorned with stars.

sanskrit: tathā bhīṣmakṛpadroṇaśalyaduryodhanādibhiḥ tavāpi vibabhau senā grahair dyaur iva saṃvṛtā
english: And likewise your army, with Bhīṣma, Kṛpa, Droṇa, Śalya, Duryodhana, and the rest, blazed forth like the sky thick-set with planets.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu kaunteyo droṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā parākramī abhyayāj javanair aśvair bhāradvājasya vāhinīm
english: But the valiant son of Kuntī, Bhīmasena, seeing Droṇa, drove with swift horses against the host of Bhāradvāja.

sanskrit: droṇas tu samare kruddho bhīmaṃ navabhir āyasaiḥ vivyādha samare rājan marmāṇy uddiśya vīryavān
english: But Droṇa, enraged in the fight, the valorous one, pierced Bhīma in battle with nine iron shafts, aiming at his vital parts, O king.

sanskrit: dṛḍhāhatas tato bhīmo bhāradvājasya saṃyuge sārathiṃ preṣayām āsa yamasya sadanaṃ prati
english: Then Bhīma, struck hard in the combat, sent the charioteer of Bhāradvāja off to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: sa saṃgṛhya svayaṃ vāhān bhāradvājaḥ pratāpavān vyadhamat pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ tūlarāśim ivānalaḥ
english: Then the mighty Bhāradvāja, taking the reins of his horses himself, scattered the Pāṇḍava army as fire consumes a heap of cotton.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānā droṇena bhīṣmeṇa ca narottama sṛñjayāḥ kekayaiḥ sārdhaṃ palāyanaparābhavan
english: Cut down by Droṇa and by Bhīṣma, O best of men, the Sṛñjayas together with the Kekayas turned and fled in defeat.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ bhīmārjunaparikṣatam muhyate tatra tatraiva samadeva varāṅganā
english: In the same way your army, mangled by Bhīma and Arjuna, swooned here and there, like a lovely woman overcome with wine.

sanskrit: abhidyetāṃ tato vyūhau tasmin vīravarakṣaye āsīd vyatikaro ghoras tava teṣāṃ ca bhārata
english: Then both formations were broken apart in that destruction of the foremost heroes, and a terrible confusion arose between your men and theirs, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tad adbhutam apaśyāma tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha ekāyanagatāḥ sarve yad ayudhyanta bhārata
english: We beheld this marvel of your warriors locked with the foe, O Bhārata: how all of them, brought to a single narrow path, fought on.

sanskrit: pratisaṃvārya cāstrāṇi te 'nyonyasya viśāṃ pate yuyudhuḥ pāṇḍavāś caiva kauravāś ca mahārathāḥ
english: Warding off one another's weapons, O lord of peoples, the great chariot-warriors of both Pāṇḍavas and Kauravas fought hand to hand.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca evaṃ bahuguṇaṃ sainyam evaṃ bahuvidhaṃ param vyūḍham evaṃ yathāśāstram amoghaṃ caiva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: An army so rich in excellences, so manifold and supreme, arrayed thus according to the science of war, and unfailing too, O Saṃjaya—

sanskrit: puṣṭam asmākam atyantam abhikāmaṃ ca naḥ sadā prahvam avyasanopetaṃ purastād dṛṣṭavikramam
english: Exceedingly well-provisioned, ever devoted to our cause, obedient, free of vice, its valor proven in former days—

sanskrit: nātivṛddham abālaṃ ca na kṛśaṃ na ca pīvaram laghuvṛttāyataprāyaṃ sāragātram anāmayam
english: Neither too old nor too young, neither lean nor gross, for the most part lithe and tall of limb, sinewy of body and free of disease—

sanskrit: āttasaṃnāhaśastraṃ ca bahuśastraparigraham asiyuddhe niyuddhe ca gadāyuddhe ca kovidam
english: Equipped with armor and weapons, furnished with weapons in abundance, skilled in sword-combat, in wrestling, and in fighting with the mace—

sanskrit: prāsarṣṭitomareṣv ājau parigheṣv āyaseṣu ca bhiṇḍipāleṣu śaktīṣu musaleṣu ca sarvaśaḥ
english: In battle skilled with the lance, the spear, and the javelin, with iron bludgeons, with slings, with darts, and with pestle-clubs, in every kind—

sanskrit: kampaneṣu ca cāpeṣu kaṇapeṣu ca sarvaśaḥ kṣepaṇīṣu ca citrāsu muṣṭiyuddheṣu kovidam
english: With the kampana, with the bow, and with the barbed kaṇapa in every form, with the wondrous catapult-slings, and skilled in fist-fighting too—

sanskrit: aparokṣaṃ ca vidyāsu vyāyāmeṣu kṛtaśramam śastragrahaṇavidyāsu sarvāsu pariniṣṭhitam
english: Versed firsthand in the sciences, trained hard in martial exercises, and accomplished in every art of wielding weapons—

sanskrit: ārohe paryavaskande saraṇe sāntaraplute samyakpraharaṇe yāne vyapayāne ca kovidam
english: Skilled in mounting, in leaping aside, in advancing, in springing across the intervening space, in striking aright, in charging, and in withdrawing—

sanskrit: nāgāśvarathayāneṣu bahuśaḥ suparīkṣitam parīkṣya ca yathānyāyaṃ vetanenopapāditam
english: Many times well-tested in the handling of elephants, horses, and chariots, and, after due examination, provided with its wages in proper measure—

sanskrit: na goṣṭhyā nopacāreṇa na ca bandhunimittataḥ na sauhṛdabalaiś cāpi nākulīnaparigrahaiḥ
english: Not through mere fellowship, nor through favor, nor on account of kinship, nor through the force of friendship, nor by the recruiting of low-born men—

sanskrit: samṛddhajanam āryaṃ ca tuṣṭasatkṛtabāndhavam kṛtopakārabhūyiṣṭhaṃ yaśasvi ca manasvi ca
english: Composed of prosperous, noble men, whose kinsmen were contented and well-honored, men richly bound by past favors, renowned and high of spirit—

sanskrit: sajayaiś ca narair mukhyair bahuśo mukhyakarmabhiḥ lokapālopamais tāta pālitaṃ lokaviśrutaiḥ
english: Guarded by victorious, foremost men of many a foremost deed, like unto the guardians of the world, my son, and famed throughout the earth—

sanskrit: bahubhiḥ kṣatriyair guptaṃ pṛthivyāṃ lokasaṃmataiḥ asmān abhigataiḥ kāmāt sabalaiḥ sapadānugaiḥ
english: Protected by many Kṣatriyas honored across the world, who had come to us of their own free will with their troops and their retainers—

sanskrit: mahodadhim ivāpūrṇam āpagābhiḥ samantataḥ apakṣaiḥ pakṣasaṃkāśai rathair nāgaiś ca saṃvṛtam
english: Like the great ocean filled on every side by rivers, encompassed by chariots and elephants that, though wingless, seemed to bear wings—

sanskrit: nānāyodhajalaṃ bhīmaṃ vāhanormitaraṅgiṇam kṣepaṇyasigadāśaktiśaraprāsasamākulam
english: That dreadful sea whose waters were its varied warriors, whose surging waves were its mounts, thronged with slings, swords, maces, spears, arrows, and lances—

sanskrit: dhvajabhūṣaṇasaṃbādhaṃ ratnapaṭṭena saṃcitam vāhanaiḥ parisarpadbhir vāyuvegavikampitam
english: Close-packed with banners and ornaments, heaped with jeweled cloth, set astir by its coursing mounts as by the rush of the wind—

sanskrit: apāram iva garjantaṃ sāgarapratimaṃ mahat droṇabhīṣmābhisaṃguptaṃ guptaṃ ca kṛtavarmaṇā
english: Roaring as though shoreless, vast and like unto the sea, well-shielded by Droṇa and Bhīṣma, and guarded by Kṛtavarman—

sanskrit: kṛpaduḥśāsanābhyāṃ ca jayadrathamukhais tathā bhagadattavikarṇābhyāṃ drauṇisaubalabāhlikaiḥ
english: And by Kṛpa and Duḥśāsana, and by the warriors led by Jayadratha, by Bhagadatta and Vikarṇa, by the son of Droṇa, by the son of Subala, and by Bāhlika—

sanskrit: guptaṃ pravīrair lokasya sāravadbhir mahātmabhiḥ yad ahanyata saṃgrāme diṣṭam etat purātanam
english: Guarded by the world's foremost heroes, steadfast and great of soul—that such an army should be cut down in battle, this is the working of an ancient fate.

sanskrit: naitādṛśaṃ samudyogaṃ dṛṣṭavanto 'tha mānuṣāḥ ṛṣayo vā mahābhāgāḥ purāṇā bhuvi saṃjaya
english: Never had men beheld a martial array such as this, nor even the blessed sages of old upon the earth, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: īdṛśo hi balaughas tu yuktaḥ śastrāstrasaṃpadā vadhyate yatra saṃgrāme kim anyad bhāgadheyataḥ
english: When so vast a flood of force, furnished with the wealth of weapons and missiles, is slain in battle, what can this be but the work of destiny?

sanskrit: viparītam idaṃ sarvaṃ pratibhāti sma saṃjaya yatredṛśaṃ balaṃ ghoraṃ nātarad yudhi pāṇḍavān
english: All this appears to me turned upside down, O Saṃjaya, in that so terrible a host could not overcome the Pāṇḍavas in the fight.

sanskrit: atha vā pāṇḍavārthāya devās tatra samāgatāḥ yudhyante māmakaṃ sainyaṃ yad avadhyanta saṃjaya
english: Or else the gods have gathered there for the Pāṇḍavas' sake and do battle against my army—and so it is being slain, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: ukto hi vidureṇeha hitaṃ pathyaṃ ca saṃjaya na ca gṛhṇāti tan mandaḥ putro duryodhano mama
english: For Vidura spoke counsel here that was salutary and wholesome, O Saṃjaya; yet my dull-witted son Duryodhana would not take it to heart.

sanskrit: tasya manye matiḥ pūrvaṃ sarvajñasya mahātmanaḥ āsīd yathāgataṃ tāta yena dṛṣṭam idaṃ purā
english: I think that the mind of that all-knowing, great-souled one was set, even beforehand, upon what was foreordained, my son—for he had foreseen all this long ago.

sanskrit: atha vā bhāvyam evaṃ hi saṃjayaitena sarvathā purā dhātrā yathā sṛṣṭaṃ tat tathā na tad anyathā
english: Or else, O Saṃjaya, all this was bound by every means to come to pass: as the Ordainer fashioned it of old, so it is, and not otherwise.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca ātmadoṣāt tvayā rājan prāptaṃ vyasanam īdṛśam na hi duryodhanas tāni paśyate bharatarṣabha yāni tvaṃ dṛṣṭavān rājan dharmasaṃkarakārite
english: Saṃjaya said: Through your own fault, O king, has such a calamity come upon you; for Duryodhana does not see, O bull of the Bharatas, those things which you saw, O king, when the confounding of righteousness was wrought.

sanskrit: tava doṣāt purā vṛttaṃ dyūtam etad viśāṃ pate tava doṣeṇa yuddhaṃ ca pravṛttaṃ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ tvam evādya phalaṃ bhuṅkṣva kṛtvā kilbiṣam ātmanā
english: Through your fault that game of dice took place long ago, O lord of peoples; through your fault this war with the Pāṇḍavas began. Now reap the fruit yourself, having wrought the evil by your own hand.

sanskrit: ātmanā hi kṛtaṃ karma ātmanaivopabhujyate iha vā pretya vā rājaṃs tvayā prāptaṃ yathātatham
english: For the deed that one does oneself is by oneself enjoyed, whether here or hereafter, O king; and this has come upon you exactly as it was earned.

sanskrit: tasmād rājan sthiro bhūtvā prāpyedaṃ vyasanaṃ mahat śṛṇu yuddhaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ śaṃsato mama māriṣa
english: Therefore, O king, having met with this great calamity, make yourself steadfast and hear the battle as it befell, while I recount it, O honored one.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu niśitair bāṇair bhittvā mahācamūm āsasāda tato vīraḥ sarvān duryodhanānujān
english: Bhīmasena, having cleft the great host with his whetted arrows, then, that hero, fell upon all the younger brothers of Duryodhana.

sanskrit: duḥśāsanaṃ durviṣahaṃ duḥsahaṃ durmadaṃ jayam jayatsenaṃ vikarṇaṃ ca citrasenaṃ sudarśanam
english: Duḥśāsana, Durviṣaha, Duḥsaha, Durmada, Jaya, Jayatsena, Vikarṇa, Citrasena, Sudarśana—

sanskrit: cārucitraṃ suvarmāṇaṃ duṣkarṇaṃ karṇam eva ca etān anyāṃś ca subahūn samīpasthān mahārathān
english: Cārucitra, Suvarman, Duṣkarṇa, and Karṇa as well—these and many other great chariot-warriors standing near at hand.

sanskrit: dhārtarāṣṭrān susaṃkruddhān dṛṣṭvā bhīmo mahābalaḥ bhīṣmeṇa samare guptāṃ praviveśa mahācamūm
english: Seeing the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra in furious wrath, the mighty Bhīma plunged into that great host shielded in battle by Bhīṣma.

sanskrit: athāhvayanta te 'nyonyam ayaṃ prāpto vṛkodaraḥ jīvagrāhaṃ nigṛhṇīmo vayam enaṃ narādhipāḥ
english: Then they called to one another: Here has Vṛkodara come! Let us seize him alive, we kings, and take him captive!

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛtaḥ pārtho bhrātṛbhiḥ kṛtaniścayaiḥ prajāsaṃharaṇe sūryaḥ krūrair iva mahāgrahaiḥ
english: Pārtha, ringed about by those resolute brothers, was like the Sun at the dissolution of all creatures, hemmed in by the cruel great planets.

sanskrit: saṃprāpya madhyaṃ vyūhasya na bhīḥ pāṇḍavam āviśat yathā devāsure yuddhe mahendraḥ prāpya dānavān
english: Having reached the very midst of the formation, no fear entered the Pāṇḍava, even as it entered not the great Indra when he met the Dānavas in the war of gods and demons.

sanskrit: tataḥ śatasahasrāṇi rathināṃ sarvaśaḥ prabho chādayānaṃ śarair ghorais tam ekam anuvavrire
english: Then hundreds of thousands of chariot-warriors on every side, O lord, hemmed in that single man, covering him with their dreadful shafts.

sanskrit: sa teṣāṃ pravarān yodhān hastyaśvarathasādinaḥ jaghāna samare śūro dhārtarāṣṭrān acintayan
english: That hero, heedless of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, slew in battle their foremost fighters—the elephant-riders, the horsemen, and the chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ vyavasitaṃ jñātvā bhīmaseno jighṛkṣatām samastānāṃ vadhe rājan matiṃ cakre mahāmanāḥ
english: Knowing the resolve of those who sought to take him captive, the great-minded Bhīmasena set his mind, O king, upon the slaughter of them all.

sanskrit: tato rathaṃ samutsṛjya gadām ādāya pāṇḍavaḥ jaghāna dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ taṃ balaughamahārṇavam
english: Then, forsaking his chariot and taking up his mace, the Pāṇḍava smote that vast ocean which was the flood of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's host.

sanskrit: bhīmasene praviṣṭe tu dhṛṣṭadyumno 'pi pārṣataḥ droṇam utsṛjya tarasā prayayau yatra saubalaḥ
english: When Bhīmasena had plunged in, Dhṛṣṭadyumna too, the son of Pṛṣata, leaving Droṇa, set out in haste for where the son of Subala was.
